title: Prerequisite Propagation Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Prerequisite Propagation
Learning Graph
Mastery Threshold
Gap Analysis
description: A vis-network explorer of a seven-concept prerequisite graph in which learners read per-concept mastery estimates, walk depends-on edges upstream and find the deepest unmastered prerequisite, distinguishing a concept's own weak evidence from weakness inherited from a prerequisite.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Prerequisite gap analysis on a learning graph
learningObjectives: Differentiate a struggling concept whose own evidence is weak from one whose weakness traces to an unmastered prerequisite, by walking dependency edges upstream.

accessibility.colorBlindSafePalette: ColorBrewer RdYlBu with printed values and check marks

controls.label: Click a concept node to select it

assumptions: Concepts and estimates are illustrative, not from learner data.
The first gap is the unmastered prerequisite at the greatest distance upstream of the selected concept.
Estimates are only read, matching the LRS Prerequisite Gap Analysis report.

keyQuestions: Is this concept weak because of its own evidence or because of a prerequisite?
How does the mastery threshold change which concepts count as gaps?
commonMisconceptions: A low estimate always means the concept itself must be retaught.
The gap report changes mastery estimates along the edges.
The mastery threshold is a fact about the learner rather than a policy.
assessmentOpportunities: Name the first gap for a selected concept and justify it from the edges.
Explain why Percentages and Rates receive different verdicts.
